1. Scope — Covers dimensions and requirements for parallel hand reamars with parallel shanks. 

2. Dimensions — As given in "able 1* 

3. Tolerances — Tolerance on cutting length /, parallel shank length /1 and over-all length L shall be

4. General Requirements 

4.1 Bevel Lead Angle — 45° to be concentric with the diameter of reamer within 0*03 mm. 

4.2 8acA Taper — Back taper on the cutting diameter is recommended; when provided the amount of 
back taper shall be within the limits of tolerance on the diameter. 

4.3 Flutes — Unless otherwise specified, left hand helical flutes for right hand cutting. 

4.4 Taper Lead — The taper lead shall be approximately 1° and the length of the taper shall be 
1-j- times the diameter of reamer or 20 mm whichever is smaller. r 

4.5 Long Taper Lead Reamers — When so required, long taper lead reamers similar In all respects 
to parallel hand reamers, except that the cutting edges are tapered, shall have four-fifths of the flute 
length tapered and one-fifth parallel. Sizes under 16 mm diameter shall have a taper 1 in 100 and 
sizes 16 mm diameter and above shall have a taper 1 in 75. 

4.6 The tolerance on parallel shank diameter shall be hO. 

4.7 For requirements not covered in this standard it shall conform to the requirements as given in 
IS : 5443-1969 ' Technical supply conditions for reamers \ 

5. Sampling —-The sampling and criteria of acceptance shall be In accordance with IS : 7778-1975 
1 Methods for sampling small tools '.

6. Designation — A parallel hand reamer with parallel shank having diameter (/ = 160 mm made 
from high speed steel conforming to this standard and suitable for a hole with tolerance H8 f shall 
be designated as: 

Reamer 16'0 IS: 5444 

6.1 When the reamer is required for a hole with tolerance other than H8, an appropriate hole 
tolerance shall be included in the designation after size. 

7. Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1969 and is being revised to bring it In line with work done 
at ISO level. In the present revision, the values of diameter ^ have been deleted as values of 
diameter d\ and diameter d are same. 

In the preparation of this standard considerable assistance has been drawn from ISO 236/1-1976 
4 Hand reamers • issued by the International Organization for Standardization. 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
